proposals.title: Describe financial intent in the language
proposals.bookReference: Proving Nothing, Chapter 3, ‘The Four Philosophies’ and ‘The Running Example: A Sudoku Proof’ (exact chapter excerpt L2-EXACT-CHAPTER.md). The chapter frames Layer 2 as how developers express a computation and its public/private boundary.

sourceSupport.reference: Chapter 3, ‘The Four Philosophies’; ‘The Running Example: A Sudoku Proof’
sourceSupport.note: The book presents distinct language approaches and uses a running example to distinguish public input from private witness.
The contract says developers specify invariants and transition rules, while users authorize exact outcome and authority constraints.

proposals.websiteMapping: Introduce Moriarty's language by the financial conditions a developer can express: exact assets, recipients, gross limits, fees, minimum net outcomes, authorization, and continuing duties. Keep developer-authored program rules distinct from the user's signed authorization.
proposals.readerCopy: Write the financial rules for an action: which assets may move, who may receive them, what fees and limits apply, and what duties remain afterward. The user authorizes the allowed outcome separately.
proposals.interaction: A proposed side-by-side inspector highlights program rules, user-authorized limits, and unresolved duties for a small partial-payment example. Each field links to its source expression or signed-intent item; label the display as a concept until implemented.
proposals.diagram: Program rules + signed authorization → candidate action → required proof relation → actual consumer. Add an explicit boundary between the first two inputs; mark the latter handoff as target-dependent.
questions: Which language constructs and target profiles currently express and enforce each listed financial condition?
How should a signing display explain a condition whose meaning depends on versioned semantics?
proposals.limits: The product contract states requirements and boundaries; it does not show that all constructs are implemented or accepted on Cardano. The book's Sudoku boundary is an educational example, not a Moriarty feature claim.

proposals.title: Show compiler and relation as an artifact handoff
proposals.bookReference: Proving Nothing, Chapter 3, ‘From Circuits to Virtual Machines: A Brief Evolution’; Chapter 10, ‘The Causal Web: Why It Is a DAG, Not a Stack’ (B08 exact sections, lines 4460–4479).

sourceSupport.reference: Chapter 3, ‘From Circuits to Virtual Machines’; Chapter 10, lines 4460–4479
sourceSupport.note: The book describes compiler-mediated translation and says engineering pressures connect language with lower layers; its layer ordering is pedagogical rather than a clean architecture of independent modules.
The contract requires target and compiler identities to be pinned separately and says compilation must preserve the intended relation; correspondence remains open until established.

sourceSupport.reference: integrated-r2/CONCEPT.md, ‘How an application would use a Web’
sourceSupport.note: The concept proposes an artifact-first handoff with program, semantics/compiler versions, proof identities, context, consumer, and evidence stage.

proposals.websiteMapping: Use an artifact map between source language and the named proof/consumer target. Show identifiers and evidence stage at each edge; do not imply compiler correctness from the existence of an output artifact.
proposals.readerCopy: The compiler translates a program for a named target. Its output is handed to the proof and verification parts of the system. Each handoff should identify the program, semantics, compiler, target, and evidence available for that link.
proposals.interaction: A proposed expandable handoff view lets a reader select source, compiled artifact, relation identity, proof instance, and consumer. For the current experiment it should display only fields and stages supported by the cited evidence, with unknown links marked open.
proposals.diagram: Source program → compiler/version → target artifact and relation → proof instance → named consumer → ledger outcome. Add a feedback arrow from proof/arithmetization constraints to language design, labeled ‘engineering influence’.
questions: For the current Rust/Cardano route, which exact artifact identities and correspondence links can the site show from the supplied evidence?
Which specific book statements should be presented as general taxonomy rather than as a description of Moriarty?
proposals.limits: This is an explanatory UX proposal, not a claim that a supported SDK handoff or end-to-end compiler correspondence exists. Chapter 10 describes interdependence; it does not establish a formal DAG for Moriarty.

proposals.title: Keep fees and residual duties in the language story
proposals.bookReference: Proving Nothing, Chapter 3, ‘The Running Example: A Sudoku Proof’ (exact chapter excerpt); cross-layer context from Chapter 10, lines 4460–4479.

sourceSupport.reference: S03-MORIARTY-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md, ‘What provable intention means’ and ‘Partial transactions and conditional settlement’
sourceSupport.note: The contract binds fees, gross and net outcomes, liabilities, and allowed partial completion/recovery; composition preserves residual duties.

sourceSupport.reference: integrated-r2/CONCEPT.md, ‘A first reference app that teaches the model’
sourceSupport.note: The concept proposes an invoice example in which partial payment retains duties, and distinguishes financial partial progress from missing proof evidence.

proposals.websiteMapping: Make financial meaning part of the language introduction, rather than treating a program as an abstract computation. Use one sourced partial-invoice specimen to demonstrate gross debit, fee, net payment, and remaining duty, with the source behavior and proposed policy clearly separated.
proposals.readerCopy: A partial action can pay part of an obligation and leave the rest due. Fees count toward the amount authorized, and a successful local step does not erase duties that continue afterward.
proposals.interaction: A proposed slider for a labelled invoice fixture recalculates gross debit, fee, recipient amount, and remaining duty. Clearly separate recorded source behavior from a proposed full-backing policy; do not present the calculation as executed ledger evidence.
proposals.diagram: Opening assets and duties → partial action (payment + fee) → remaining assets and duties. Show proof requirements on a parallel lane so incomplete evidence is not confused with an authorized partial financial outcome.
questions: Which partial-payment figures are approved for direct reader display, and which remain source worksheets only?
What named target evidence is required before the example can be labeled an implemented financial workflow?
proposals.limits: The contract's semantics are requirements, not proof of full implementation. The concept's invoice worksheet is source-level analysis; it is not an executed transaction or measured performance result.

proposals.title: Separate current Rust/Cardano evidence from the Midnight target
proposals.bookReference: Proving Nothing, Chapter 3, ‘The Four Philosophies’ and ‘From Circuits to Virtual Machines: A Brief Evolution’. The chapter surveys multiple language and execution approaches; Chapter 10, lines 4460–4479, cautions that the layers influence one another.

sourceSupport.note: The target architecture names Midnight ZKIRv3 and native proof infrastructure, while explicitly separating non-Midnight routes and incomplete capabilities.

sourceSupport.reference: integrated-r2/CONCEPT.md, ‘Developer experience and ecosystem delivery’ and ‘Later-source readings and their limits’
sourceSupport.note: The integrated concept proposes separate Cardano experimental and Midnight target guides and describes the Rust/Cardano route as a frozen experimental path.

proposals.websiteMapping: Give each example a visible target badge and evidence stage. Keep the current Rust/Cardano experiment distinct from the specified Midnight ZKIRv3 target. Do not use Compact or Midnight implementation details as support for the Rust/Cardano route.
proposals.readerCopy: Moriarty has separate target routes. The Rust/Cardano path described here is experimental. The specified Midnight target has its own compiler, proof, and ledger requirements. Evidence for one route does not establish the other.
proposals.interaction: A proposed target switcher changes only the explanatory artifact map and evidence labels for the selected target. If a field is unknown for that target, show ‘not established in this source’ rather than carrying it across from another route.
proposals.diagram: Shared language concepts branch into separately labeled Rust/Cardano experimental and Midnight ZKIRv3 target routes, each with its own compiler, proof interface, consumer, and evidence status.
questions: Which page and artifact currently own the authoritative current Rust/Cardano support inventory?
What is the exact maturity label and evidence path for each target-specific claim on the website?
proposals.limits: The supplied concept gives a bounded evidence summary, not a complete inventory of current support. The proposal makes no claim of Cardano deployment, verified compiler correspondence, or Midnight acceptance.
